$comment: Keel corpus — the targets the published grounding ratios are computed over.
Every revision is a pinned 40-char sha, verified with `git ls-remote <url> HEAD`
on 2026-07-24. Pinning is not bookkeeping: an unpinned corpus produces a number
nobody can reproduce, and an unreproducible number is not a result.
Order is load-bearing. corpus.ts walks this list top to bottom, sequentially, and
records the order it ran in — the crystallization curve measures probe-library
growth, so a reshuffle or a parallel run destroys the signal being measured.
Selection is a deliberate spread of verification cultures — agent/AI tools,
generated SDKs, heavily-tested infrastructure, an LLM-wrapper app, and two
docs-heavy repos with almost no CI. A corpus that is all one shape yields one
number and no insight. `keel` is first because refusing to publish your own
number is precisely the failure this project names.
RETIRED ORIGIN (2026-08-03). The `keel` target pinned github.com/broomva/keel,
which was deleted when Keel moved into broomva/skills. That target is therefore
no longer re-runnable: the tree it measured was a standalone repository with its
own Makefile, .githooks/, .control/ and workflows, and none of that shape exists
in the monorepo. The entry is kept because the published ratios and the
crystallization curve were computed over this list and removing a row would
falsify the population they describe. By this file's own standard that one
number is now unreproducible, and saying so is the only honest option — the
other 14 targets remain pinned and re-runnable.
